staff2fa.title: Require 2FA for admins
staff2fa.desc: Admins and owners without two-factor authentication can only open their own security settings until they set it up. API keys of those accounts stop working too. Only an owner with 2FA can turn this on.
staff2fa.onlyOwner: Only an owner can change this
staff2fa.stateOn: On: admins and owners must use 2FA.
staff2fa.toastOn: 2FA is now required for admins and owners
staff2fa.saveFailed: Failed to save the security policy

backupKey.title: Backup encryption
backupKey.desc: Backups are encrypted with a panel-managed key before they are written or copied off-site, so a leaked storage credential never exposes world data. Keep an exported copy of the key somewhere safe — without it, a lost panel database means unrecoverable backups.
backupKey.storeOffline: Store this offline. Anyone with this key can decrypt your backup archives.
backupKey.onlyOwner: Only the owner can reveal or rotate the backup key.
backupKey.loadFailed: Failed to load backup key status
backupKey.confirmRotate: Generate a new backup encryption key? New backups use the new key; existing backups keep restoring with their old key. Export and store the new key somewhere safe afterwards.

hytale.title: Hytale Account
hytale.desc: Link a Hytale account once and servers start authenticated, with no {cmd} in the console. Players can only join authenticated servers. Enable it per server under Settings → Launch Settings; plugins on those servers can read the session.
hytale.openLink: Open {link} and sign in with the Hytale account the servers should run as.
hytale.footnote: The refresh token is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted in {table}; each server start gets its own one-hour game session, which the server renews while running. Up to 500 servers per account. If the panel is offline for more than 30 days, link the account again.
hytale.loadFailed: Failed to load Hytale account status
hytale.startFailed: Could not start the Hytale login
hytale.profileSaved: Profile saved. Applies to the next server start.
hytale.confirmUnlink: Unlink the Hytale account? Servers will start unauthenticated from their next start on.

curseforge.desc: Required for the in-panel mod browser. Get a key at {link}.
curseforge.footnote: Stored AES-256-GCM encrypted in {table}. Takes effect immediately — no API restart required. Clearing falls back to the {env} env value (if set) on the next API restart.
curseforge.confirmClear: Clear the stored CurseForge API key? Mod browsing will stop working until a new key is provided.

smtp.title: Email (SMTP)
smtp.desc: Needed for email alerts. Enter the SMTP details from your mail provider, for example your web hosting package, Gmail with an app password, or a sending service like Brevo or Mailgun.
smtp.envNote: These values come from the {env} environment variables. Once you save here, the panel's values are used instead.
smtp.passwordSaved: Saved. Leave empty to keep it
smtp.senderHint: Most providers only accept a sender address that belongs to your account.
smtp.footnote: The test email goes to your own account's address and uses the saved settings, so save first. The password is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted in {table} and is never shown again. Changes take effect immediately, no API restart required.
smtp.confirmClear: Remove the email settings stored in the panel? Email alerts stop unless SMTP_* environment variables are set.
smtp.testSent: Test email sent to {email}. Check your inbox and spam folder.

certificates.title: Node certificates
certificates.desc: The panel and its nodes authenticate each other with certificates from the panel's own CA (mTLS). Nodes renew their certificate by themselves 30 days before it expires. Rotate the CA if its key may have leaked, or as routine hygiene.

confirm.start: Start a CA rotation? The panel creates a new CA. Nodes on TaleDaemon v0.15+ fetch a certificate from it on their next heartbeat, without a restart. The old CA stays trusted until you finish the rotation.
confirm.finish: Finish the rotation? The old CA is no longer trusted and the panel switches its own client certificate to the new CA.
confirm.force: Finish although some nodes have no certificate from the new CA? Those nodes become unreachable for the panel until they are re-enrolled (delete the daemon's PKI directory and restart it).
confirm.cancel: Cancel the rotation? The old CA becomes active again. Nodes that already renewed switch back on their next heartbeat (a few seconds without panel access).

certificates.rotationProgress: Rotation in progress · {done} of {total} nodes on the new CA
certificates.oldCaTrusted: Old CA {fp} stays trusted until you finish.
certificates.renewOnHeartbeat: Nodes renew on their next heartbeat.
certificates.oldDaemons: {n} node runs a daemon older than v0.15, which cannot follow a CA rotation. Update it before rotating. | {n} nodes run a daemon older than v0.15, which cannot follow a CA rotation. Update them before rotating.
certificates.onlyOwner: Only the owner can rotate the CA.

templates.title: Server templates
templates.desc: Presets offered when someone creates a server. A template only fills in defaults: the same rules apply as for settings chosen by hand, so a user cannot get admin-only options (such as {flag} or a network role) through a template.

flags.acceptEarlyPluginsHint: required by mods that load before the server boots
flags.allowOpHint: only admins can create servers from this template

templates.customEmpty: No custom templates yet. Create one or save the settings of an existing server.
templates.name: Name
templates.copiesNote: Copies version, RAM, CPU, disk, auto restart, crash limits, launch flags and network role. Files and worlds are not copied.
templates.pickServer: Pick a server and give the template a name
templates.confirmDelete: Delete the template "{name}"? Servers created from it are not affected.
